question: Four analysts on an Enterprise plan are running separate chats to analyse requirements for the same programme, and each keeps re-pasting the same brief, glossary and stakeholder map. What is the most appropriate improvement?
options: A) Ask each analyst to paste a shortened summary of the documents rather than the full versions each time.
B) Agree that a single analyst holds the source documents and answers the other three analysts on request each time.
C) Merge the four conversations into one long chat so the shared material has to be pasted only once.
D) Put the brief, glossary and stakeholder map into a shared project so every analysis chat starts from them.
correct_answers: D) Put the brief, glossary and stakeholder map into a shared project so every analysis chat starts from them.
explanations: Shortened summaries mean each analyst works from a different reduction of the same material, which is how definitions quietly diverge. Requirements analysis depends on everyone reading the same glossary, not four paraphrases of it.

Funnelling the documents through one person creates a bottleneck and leaves the other three analysts analysing from second-hand descriptions. It solves the duplication by removing access rather than by sharing context.

One very long shared conversation mixes four unrelated lines of analysis, becomes hard to follow, and pushes against the limits of a single chat. It also gives no way to start a fresh piece of analysis from the same background.

Correct. Recurring work over a stable set of source material is exactly what a project is for: the brief, glossary and stakeholder map become durable background for every chat in that project, so all four analysts work from the same current version instead of from whatever each last pasted.
